Tokyo Nights Coffee · October 2026

Storefront review

The new product names are live, the collections are filled, and the main shopping journey has been checked. This report covers the work completed, what turned up during the 8 October follow-up, and the decisions still needed before the work can be signed off.

The big picture

The store is taking shape. A few things still need attention.

The product renames and collection updates are live. The checks also found no changes to the supplier-linked product data.
The main concern is the three manual Core Four products. Ginza Velvet, Harajuku Heat and Shibuya Sunrise can be purchased, but their supplier fulfillment is still unconfirmed. A decision is needed on whether to keep them on sale.

The tea label and Whole Bean / Ground Coffee filter also need approval. Discovery Boxes works, but its menu position differs from the agreed layout. These items, along with the outstanding supplier questions, are why the work is not yet ready for sign-off.
Completed

What’s already done

  • All 21 approved product names are live. Their web addresses have stayed the same.
  • Seven tea descriptions now open with a line identifying the tea.
  • Shop Coffee now has 62 products: Signature Blends 17; Single Origins 17; Flavored Coffee 16; Specialty Coffee 7; Capsules 5.
  • Tokyo Tea Collection contains all 11 tea products.
  • Discovery Boxes contains exactly Tokyo Discovery Six, Tokyo Flavor Discovery and Tokyo Origins Journey.
  • Capsule/pod products are no longer in Ground Coffee; Instant Coffee is organized under Specialty Coffee.
  • Roppongi Nights remains live with its existing supplier-linked variants/SKUs.
  • US and international shipping rates appeared at checkout. No order was placed.
  • 97 checked URLs returned HTTP 200 on 7 October; the 8 October re-check of 103 URLs also returned HTTP 200 with no redirects and no 404s.
  • The 8 October mobile check used 390px and 430px iPhone-sized views in Chrome. No broken layouts or sideways page overflow were found; a physical phone was not used.
Supplier data

The supplier details are unchanged

  • Supplier-linked SKUs and variant structure remained unchanged.

  • Product handles/URLs remained unchanged during the approved title updates.
  • Existing sample-pack bundle contents remained unchanged; Tokyo Discovery Six still retains “Cowboy Blend” in its description.
  • No real checkout order was submitted.

Decisions to make

What needs a go-ahead

  • Tea display label: storefront still shows “Grind / Loose leaf”. The option originates from Dripshipper. Directly renaming the supplier-linked option may affect synchronization. The theme could show “Format: Loose Leaf” without changing the supplier option. That approach needs approval and would need to be maintained when the theme changes.
  • Whole Bean / Ground Coffee filter: shoppers can currently filter by Availability and Price only. Adding Shopify Search & Discovery needs approval; the app is not installed yet. Existing tag counts are Whole Bean 54 and Ground Coffee 60.
  • Core Four manual products: Ginza Velvet, Harajuku Heat and Shibuya Sunrise are currently purchasable. A sales decision is needed before supplier fulfillment is confirmed.
  • Discovery Boxes placement: currently inside the Shop Coffee submenu; the approved structure lists it as top-level. Needs confirmation before any menu change.
Supplier confirmation required

Questions for Dripshipper

  • Ginza Velvet, Harajuku Heat and Shibuya Sunrise: supplier match, Whole Bean/Ground support, SKU, weight and inventory synchronization.
  • Mint/Honduras: exact Shopify Product ID actively synchronized by Dripshipper. The suggested records to keep, once confirmed, are mint and honduras; neither pair has been deleted or merged.
  • Jasmine: Sakura/cherry blossom is not confirmed; title remains factual as “Jasmine”.
  • Candy Cane: the Shopify description says only “All natural flavoring”. The Dripshipper product page describes a “peppermint-style aroma” and “festive peppermint notes” but does not publish a flavor ingredient list. “Tokyo Winter Mint” was not used; the name awaits a decision.
  • Core Four sampler, Tea Discovery Box and mixed Coffee + Tea Discovery Box: supplier-managed fulfillment remains unconfirmed.
  • Cowboy Blend in Tokyo Discovery Six: the supplier listing names Cowboy Blend, but the contents of a physically delivered pack could not be confirmed from the available online information.
  • See the Supplier verification table below for what was checked, what was verified and what needs Dripshipper confirmation.

Who supplies the coffee and tea

Research only, from Dripshipper’s own website, Help Center and legal pages, plus the connected Dripshipper app and Shopify admin (read-only). No store or supplier setting was changed and nobody was contacted. Companies listed on Dripshipper’s Compare Suppliers page (dripshipper.io/compare-suppliers: Roastify, Supliful, Path Coffee Roasters, Aroma Ridge, Joe’s Garage Coffee) are Dripshipper’s competitors; none is connected to Tokyo Nights Coffee.

Who is who
  • Platform / company: Dripshipper, operated under The Doughty Organization LLC (per the App terms).
  • Actual roasters / manufacturers: Temecula Coffee Roasters (Temecula, CA 92590) and Calutech Inc / “Old Chicago” (Orland Park, IL 60462). These are partner companies, not Dripshipper itself.
  • Fulfillment location: orders ship from the roaster that owns the product (Temecula, CA or Orland Park, IL). No separate warehouse is published.
  • Registered business address: not published as such. The privacy-policy mailing addresses (Temecula, CA 92591 and the older Morgan Hill, CA 95037) are contact addresses, not proof of registration.
How Dripshipper supplies Tokyo Nights Coffee
  • Products are imported from the Dripshipper catalog into Shopify. When a customer pays, Dripshipper sends the order to the roaster, which roasts, packs your label and ships via USPS; tracking is written back to the Shopify order (Features, Connect with Shopify).
  • Confirmed for this store: the Dripshipper app is installed (Shopify admin → Apps); a “Dripshipper” app fulfillment location exists (Settings → Locations); the connected app shows the Tokyo Nights logo on the packaging step and lists 75 catalog products as “Imported”.
  • Roaster shown in the app for those 75: 64 list “Temecula, CA” (incl. Mint, Honduras, Cowboy Blend, Candy Cane, all 3 sample packs, all teas, pods and Instant Coffee); 11 list “Illinois, USA” (12/60 Pack Capsules, Cold Brew Coffee, Latin American, Asian Plateau, African Kahawa, House and Breakfast Blend, Gourmet Donut Shop, French Roast, Italian Roast).
Details the sources did not settle: the registered legal address and state registration of The Doughty Organization LLC; a support phone number; which of the two published mailing addresses is current; that the app label “Illinois, USA” refers specifically to Calutech Inc (the Help Center and Our Coffee page point to Orland Park, IL, but the app does not name the company); the tea packing facility; farm-level sourcing. This general company information does not prove that any particular Tokyo Nights product is linked to a particular supplier record.
Questions to take to Dripshipper: Core Four supplier matches (Ginza Velvet, Harajuku Heat, Shibuya Sunrise) — unconfirmed · Mint/Honduras exact linked Shopify Product ID — unconfirmed · Cowboy Blend physical sampler contents — unconfirmed · future custom Discovery Boxes fulfillment — unconfirmed · Jasmine Sakura ingredient — unconfirmed · Candy Cane peppermint notes documented, exact flavoring ingredient unconfirmed · effect of future syncs on custom family tags — unconfirmed. Contact for these: support@dripshipper.io or “Contact support” on dripshipper.io/contact-us.
Navigation note

Where Discovery Boxes sits in the menu

Re-checked 8 October on desktop and mobile. The live header shows Home · Shop Coffee · Tokyo Tea Collection · Contact Us. The Shop Coffee submenu shows Signature Blends · Single Origins · Flavored Coffee · Discovery Boxes · Specialty Coffee · Capsules. The approved structure is Home · Shop Coffee · Tokyo Tea Collection · Discovery Boxes · Contact Us, so the current placement does not match: Discovery Boxes is in the submenu, not top-level. The Discovery Boxes collection itself works and contains exactly three products. The menu was not changed; moving Discovery Boxes to the top level needs confirmation. On desktop, adding a fifth top-level item will likely make the header wrap further (Contact Us already wraps).
